meta.name: FavorBank
meta.notes: Color themes: light + dark (dark derived for catalog matrix). Wallpaper variants skipped. Expand with live captures on next skill run.

targetConsumers.persona: Partner who wants fair chore reciprocity

positioning.oneLiner: Private two-person favors — make effort visible, redeem what matters.
positioning.differentiator: Exactly two people; spouse-priced rewards — not family chore charts.

objectionsAndAnswers.answer: It replaces fuzzy resentment with agreed points and rewards you both chose.

features.name: Partner home & balances
features.why: Makes effort visible at a glance — points and open work without nagging.
features.howToUse: Open Home to see balances and jump into tasks or favors.
features.marketingHook: See what each of you owes — without the scorekeeping fight.

features.name: Tasks
features.why: Concrete assignments with points turn vague chore talks into clear asks.
features.howToUse: Create a task, set points, assign to your partner.

features.name: Create task
features.why: Frictionless creation keeps the bank alive day to day.
features.howToUse: Tasks → New; set 1–100 points and due intent.
features.marketingHook: Turn “can you…?” into a fair favor.

features.name: Favors & rewards
features.why: Redeeming spouse-offered rewards is the emotional payoff loop.
features.howToUse: Browse Favors, redeem when you have points, fulfill when claimed.
features.marketingHook: Rewards you both chose — not a generic points store.

features.name: Ideas / suggestions
features.why: Partners can propose offers; pricing keeps reciprocity honest.
features.howToUse: Suggest an idea; partner prices or accepts into the library.
features.marketingHook: Propose what would actually feel good.

features.name: Fulfillment
features.why: Closing the loop on redeemed favors builds trust in the system.
features.howToUse: Complete fulfilled favors from the Fulfillment queue.
features.marketingHook: Deliver what you promised — then clear the board.

features.name: History ledger
features.why: A shared ledger settles “I always do more” with receipts, not memory.
features.howToUse: Open History to review point events.
features.marketingHook: The quiet record that ends the tally argument.

features.name: Partner invite
features.why: Exactly two people — invite is the product boundary.
features.howToUse: Invite by phone/code during onboarding or Partner.
features.marketingHook: Built for two. Not a group chat chore app.

features.name: Onboarding & love languages
features.why: Sets tone and preference context before the first task.
features.marketingHook: Start with how you give — then bank the favors.

features.name: Account & appearance
features.why: Light/dark and wallpapers make daily use feel personal.
features.howToUse: Account → appearance; toggle theme or wallpaper.

features.name: Tasks I created
features.why: Outbound asks need a separate view so creators can follow up.
features.howToUse: Open Tasks I created to manage what you assigned.
features.marketingHook: Track the favors you put into the world.

features.name: Phone OTP auth
features.why: Friction-light private login matches a couples app threat model.
features.howToUse: Sign in with phone + SMS code.
features.marketingHook: Private by default — just the two of you.

features.name: Wallpapers
features.why: Delight without clutter; seasonal presets keep the app fresh.
features.marketingHook: A little atmosphere for everyday kindness.

features.name: Points economy (1–100)
features.why: Bounded points keep valuation fair and gameable-but-kind.
features.howToUse: Set points when creating tasks or pricing suggestions.

features.name: Rewards library
features.why: Saved offers become a menu of meaningful redemptions.
features.howToUse: Use the Library tab inside Favors.
features.marketingHook: A menu of favors worth redeeming.
